assigned.title: The watchlist harness reads a rate-limited sign-UP as a wrong password
assigned.acceptance:
THE OBSERVATION, WHICH IS FACT. CI run 37036128012 at 2c037d54ed834af9dba3c6b12a29c395dee81b9d: the e2e job failed, PRODUCTION mode only, 1 failed / 75 passed / 31 skipped, on 'tests/watchlist.spec.ts:859:7 - the list page, against a real session and a real database - a signed-in viewer with no profile selected is sent to the picker, not to an error'. The annotation is the harness's own message: 'the harness could not sign in as e2e-watchlist-unchosen-0@liberty.invalid: 401 {"message":"Invalid email or password","code":"INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD"}'. The DEVELOPMENT run in the same job passed, 93 passed / 14 skipped. The same spec passed in production on the previous run, 37028642916 at 30cef6e, 76 passed / 31 skipped, and nothing between those two commits touches authentication, the harness or the spec -- so it is intermittent rather than a break.

THE DEFECT IN THE HARNESS, WHICH IS ALSO FACT AND IS VISIBLE IN THE SOURCE REGARDLESS OF WHAT CAUSED THIS RUN. `signIn` in that file POSTs /api/auth/sign-up/email with failOnStatusCode: false and never looks at the response -- the comment says the sign-in is what decides, 'because a session is what the caller asked for and an account is only the way to get one'. It then retries the SIGN-IN on 429 up to four times and on nothing else. So a sign-up that was refused leaves no account, the sign-in that follows correctly answers 401 INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD because better-auth does not distinguish an unknown user from a wrong password, and the harness reports a credential failure for an account that was never created. The retry loop makes this worse rather than better: it waits out a rate-limit window and then re-asks a question whose answer cannot change.
REQUIRED: a sign-up that fails is OBSERVED and reported as itself. A 401 must not be the error text for 'the account does not exist'.
REQUIRED: whatever retry the sign-up is given is the same client-correctness retry the sign-in already has -- obeying a 429 and its retry-after. playwright.config.ts's rule stands: no ASSERTION is retried, retries stay 0, and the fix must not be `retries: 1` on the project.
REQUIRED: the diagnosis is CONFIRMED before the repair is called a repair. The hypothesis in the notes is a hypothesis.
REQUIRED: the repair is demonstrated against the production + real PostgreSQL configuration, which is the only one that failed; a development-mode pass proves nothing here, because that is the configuration that was already green.

OUT OF SCOPE AND MUST NOT BE DONE: deleting or skipping the test, relaxing its assertion, serialising the project, raising a timeout, or changing the application's authentication configuration to make the harness's traffic acceptable. The product's rate limiting is a security property; a test harness that trips it is the harness's problem.
assigned.notes:
FILED IN ROUND 107 from CI run 37036128012. NOT CAUSED BY THIS ROUND'S WORK: the delta from the last green e2e is one apps/desktop packaging script, two coordination documents and control-plane state.

THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS, LABELLED AS ONE BECAUSE IT HAS NOT BEEN CONFIRMED. packages/auth/src/better-auth.ts passes no `rateLimit` option, so better-auth's default applies -- and that default is ENABLED IN PRODUCTION AND DISABLED IN DEVELOPMENT, which is exactly the split this failure shows. If the per-path default on the sign-up endpoint is short-windowed, several Playwright workers establishing sessions in parallel would exceed it, the refused sign-up would be swallowed by the code above, and the sign-in would answer 401. That fits every observed fact and is still a guess: nobody has watched the sign-up endpoint return 429 under this harness. Confirm it by observation before building on it, and if it is wrong, say so and file what was actually found.

SHAPE NOTE. This is PL-0713 again in a different costume -- a harness that works at one worker and one machine and reports a product failure when the schedule changes. The lesson PL-0713 recorded applies: the repair is structural isolation, not a retry.

CONFLICTS, BOTH FIELDS BOTH DIRECTIONS, AT FILING. e2e/tests/watchlist.spec.ts is in PW-0304's and PW-0313's allowedPaths and both are DONE; e2e/** was PL-0501's and it is DONE. e2e/src/identity.ts is PW-0312's, DONE. No open task holds any of these in either field. The active tasks at filing are PW-0208 (REVIEW), PW-0602 (IN_PROGRESS) and PL-0714 (IN_PROGRESS), and none names an e2e path.

ROUND 108 SURFACE AMENDMENT, recorded as an event before any write: e2e/src/identity.ts moved from reviewDependencies to allowedPaths. The production reproduction at 4 workers failed on HARNESS_ACCOUNT in that file, not on the watchlist slot -- the two carry the identical defect, and repairing only the one CI happened to show would leave the one that actually reproduces.

typecheck.evidence: e2e/ npx tsc --noEmit: clean, after both files changed. Two type imports added (APIResponse in each); nothing else in the harness's types moved.

e2e.evidence:
THE DIAGNOSIS WAS CONFIRMED BEFORE THE REPAIR WAS CALLED A REPAIR, which the acceptance requires, and the confirmation moved the fix.

READ OUT OF THE INSTALLED LIBRARY. better-auth 1.7.5, dist/context/create-context.mjs line 172: `enabled: options.rateLimit?.enabled ?? isProduction` -- rate limiting is ON in production and OFF in development, which is exactly the split the CI failure showed. dist/api/rate-limiter/index.mjs getDefaultSpecialRules: window 10 seconds, max 3, for any path beginning /sign-in or /sign-up, keyed per IP and path. packages/auth/src/better-auth.ts passes no rateLimit option, so that default is what the application runs.

REPRODUCED, in the configuration the acceptance names as decisive. Production mode, real PostgreSQL 16 on 127.0.0.1:5433 with the repository migration applied, COLD DATABASE so every worker must create its account, --workers=4, full chromium+api suite: 12 failed, and the auth failure is "the harness could not sign in as e2e-harness-2@liberty.invalid: 401 INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD". A single-worker run of the same suite passes, which is why this was invisible on a two-core machine -- the same thing that hid PL-0713.

THE REPRODUCTION MOVED THE REPAIR, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH READING. The failing account is e2e-harness-2, which is src/identity.ts's HARNESS_ACCOUNT -- NOT the watchlist slot CI happened to hit. The two files carry the identical defect line for line. Fixing only the one named in the CI annotation would have left the one that actually reproduces here. The surface was amended to include e2e/src/identity.ts, recorded as an event before the write and conflict-checked in both fields in both directions.

THE REPAIR, IN BOTH FILES.
  - SIGN IN FIRST. A database that already has the account costs one request and the burst never happens. This is the change that removes the pressure rather than tolerating it.
  - The sign-up response is OBSERVED. "Already exists" is treated as success -- the account this harness needs is there either way -- and every other refusal throws, naming that the account does not exist so that nothing downstream is about a password.
  - A 429 is obeyed on BOTH endpoints, honouring X-Retry-After, on the same bounded budget the sign-in already had. SIGN_IN_ATTEMPTS was NOT raised.
  - Every attempt is logged and the log is in the failure message, so the next occurrence names itself.

THE REGRESSION RUN, SAME DECISIVE CONFIGURATION. Production mode, real PostgreSQL, cold database, --workers=4, full chromium+api suite: 77 PASSED, 41 skipped, 0 FAILED. No sign-in failure of any kind. Development mode, full suite: 103 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE, EACH FORBIDDEN BY THE ACCEPTANCE AND NONE OF THEM TEMPTING ONCE THE CAUSE WAS KNOWN: no test deleted or skipped, no assertion relaxed, no project serialised, no timeout raised, no retry count changed -- playwright.config.ts is untouched and `retries` is still 0 -- and NOTHING in the application's rate limiting was configured, relaxed or disabled. Obeying a 429 is correct client behaviour; the file says so at length, and it is the server stating a protocol requirement rather than an assertion being re-evaluated.

A FINDING FOR THE BOARD, NOT FIXED HERE: the application's auth rate limiting is better-auth's UNEXAMINED DEFAULT. Nobody chose 3-per-10-seconds, nobody chose that it is off in development, and docs/SECURITY.md residual risk R2 still says "No rate limit on any route". PL-0716 corrected the readiness item to say so precisely; deciding what the limit SHOULD be is a security task that does not exist yet.

recommended.title: Install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall — tested, not assumed
recommended.acceptance: The installer's lifecycle is exercised automatically wherever that is possible on a runner, and everything that is not is named for the commander's machine. REQUIRED: clean install on a machine that has never had the application, then launch. REQUIRED: upgrade over a previous version with user data preserved, which is the one a release breaks most often and nobody tests. REQUIRED: uninstall leaves no service, no scheduled task and no orphaned node.exe, and states exactly what user data it keeps or removes. REQUIRED: reinstall after uninstall. REQUIRED: each case is marked automated or commander-machine, with the reason, so the split is visible rather than implied.
recommended.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written.

review.evidence: CHANGES REQUESTED at 835823561c69f5bbdebf19c637eeeabff19dacf7. Transcribed by claude-lead from gpt-architect's round-105 ruling, section 2, which is a request for changes in substance even though it does not use the word: 'The lifecycle harness architecture is accepted. DO NOT mark PW-0503 DONE merely to free the Test lane. Current Windows evidence establishes only part of the lifecycle matrix.' gpt's itemised verdict: F1 clean install PARTIAL PASS -- the MSI builds, installs and its installed tree is verified; still unverified is actual installed application launch and WebView runtime. F2 upgrade UNVERIFIED -- no real previous release has been exercised as an upgrade source, so user-data preservation across an actual upgrade remains unproven. F3 uninstall PARTIAL PASS -- msiexec uninstall executes; still to prove where automation permits are no orphaned service, no scheduled task, no orphaned node.exe, expected files removed, and documented user-data retention behaviour. F4 reinstall UNVERIFIED but AUTOMATABLE -- 'implement and execute this rather than classifying it as commander-only'. WHAT HAS CHANGED SINCE THAT VERDICT WAS WRITTEN, and it narrows the request rather than answering it: the IMPLEMENTATION of F3's residue classification and of F4 reinstall already exists in scripts/windows/lifecycle.mjs and residue.mjs at the commit above, with 30 cases behind the decisions, and F4 is already marked plannedAutomated with no manual portion. What does not exist is EXECUTION, and it cannot be created by any open task: no open task can write .github/workflows/windows.yml -- every writer is DONE and PW-0502, PW-0503 and PW-0602 hold it read-only. That is recorded as a board.sequencing_finding and needs a ruling on which task gets the write surface. Recorded so the task leaves REVIEW honestly rather than being completed on evidence gpt declined to accept.
